## Summary **Defects found:** The only accessibility gaps in this page were the four `` elements missing `alt` attributes, which is an `image-alt` (WCAG 1.1.1) violation under axe-core. Everything else already met the contract: - Single `

`, proper `header`/`main` landmarks, `lang="en"`, no zoom-blocking viewport meta. - Text color contrast (`p.sub`, `figcaption`, `a.browse`) all exceed 4.5:1 against the white background. - The only interactive element, the "Browse the full catalog" link, is a native `` — reachable by Tab in reading order, activates on Enter by default, and has no CSS suppressing its default focus outline. - No dialogs or custom widgets exist on this page, so focus-trap/inert/ARIA-pattern requirements don't apply here. **Changes made:** - Added descriptive `alt` text to the three artwork photos (e.g. *"Print with a cream circle centered on a deep green field."*) so screen reader users get a sense of the visual content, which the figcaptions (title/edition only) don't convey. - Added `alt=""` to the purely decorative dot divider so it's skipped by assistive technology instead of being announced as an unlabeled image. **Left alone:** All `data-track` attributes, the instrumentation script, ids, visual design/CSS, and text content are untouched. The `href="#top"` fragment (which doesn't match an element id) was left as-is since it's a functional/content choice, not an accessibility defect — it behaves identically for mouse and keyboard users. No further edits were needed to satisfy the axe-core tag set (wcag2a/aa, wcag21a/aa, best-practice) or the keyboard-operability requirements in the contract.
